ProofLedger: evidence-grounded AI for dispute review

A sandbox workspace that links orders, logistics events, messages, and refund requests into a traceable case, then generates a bounded AI recommendation for human confirmation.

Project typeIndependent product
RoleProduct, architecture, full-stack
DomainDispute evidence review
DeliveryOpen-source repository

Background and goal

Commerce disputes often spread relevant facts across order records, shipment events, customer messages, and refund requests. ProofLedger does not make the final decision. It organises imports, deterministic evidence linkage, rule-based analysis, an evidence-restricted AI recommendation, and human confirmation into one traceable workflow.

Product boundary: the current version accepts synthetic or anonymised data and does not connect to Shopify, Stripe, carriers, or payment platforms. It cannot issue refunds, reject claims, transfer money, or send external notifications.

My responsibilities

Independently delivered

  • Defined the product goal, sandbox data boundary, and human-decision model.
  • Designed the Next.js, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, and PostgreSQL architecture.
  • Implemented preview/confirm imports, mapping, validation, de-duplication, and versioned records.
  • Built deterministic evidence linkage, conflict handling, completeness scoring, and the review queue.
  • Implemented structured AI output, evidence-ID validation, controlled tools, human review, versioned Case Briefs, and audit events.

Controlled boundaries

  • Scores prioritise review; they do not decide an outcome.
  • AI can recommend actions only from case evidence and cannot invoke payment tools.
  • Ambiguous, unmatched, and conflicting links remain outside the normal queue.
  • No production-availability claim is made before deployment and monitoring.

Technology stack

Core capabilities

  • Two-stage imports: preview and confirm flows for orders, shipment events, customer messages, and refund requests.
  • Versioned traceability: file SHA-256, row validation, duplicate provenance, normalised content hashes, and versioned business records.
  • Evidence linkage: deterministic joins with explicit linked, ambiguous, unmatched, and conflicting states.
  • Review prioritisation: explainable evidence-completeness scoring and queue filters for human operations.
  • Bounded AI: structured recommendations must cite in-case evidence and disclose contradictions, missing information, and required human checks.
  • Human closure: reviewers may confirm, request evidence, or escalate; only confirmation creates a new versioned Case Brief.

System architecture

Next.js WorkspaceRESTFastAPISQLPostgreSQL
Import & Linking→Deterministic Rules+Structured AI
Review Queue→Human Review→Case Brief + Audit

Deterministic code owns timelines, links, conflicts, and scores. The model summarises only supplied evidence and its references are validated.

Technical challenges and solutions

Imports must not overwrite business facts

I split ingestion into preview and confirmation. Preview stores mapping and row validation; confirmation creates versioned records with hashes and idempotency controls.

Cross-source relationships may be uncertain

Deterministic keys and fallback rules preserve the linking method. Ambiguous, missing, or conflicting results are routed separately instead of silently accepted.

AI must remain inside case evidence

A structured contract, case-scoped tools, evidence-ID rejection, tool traces, and mandatory human_review_required keep the model within the review boundary.

Confirmed briefs must remain stable

Each Case Brief captures a versioned snapshot. Later imports or analyses create a new version rather than mutating confirmed content.

Validation

  • The repository includes 40 API test functions covering timelines, conflicts, evidence scope, versioning, imports, de-duplication, linkage, scoring, review, snapshots, and controlled tools.
  • A deterministic fake provider supports a Golden Set for schema compliance, citation validity, contradiction and missing-evidence recall, human-review requirements, and hallucination boundaries. It is not presented as proof of live-model accuracy.
